name: Naba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog naba1253 lists only Bombay 2010 (sociolinguistic survey); no phonological description of Naba (Chad) located online

new_statements.quote: Naba is a tonal language, with three level tones, High (H), Mid (M) and Low (L). The majority of words, especially nouns and verbs, have an underlying tone melody which consists either of one level tone or a sequence of levels. However, a good number of grammatical function morphemes, such as clitics, particles, and verbal affixes, are underlyingly toneless. [p. 95] ... From the examples in the right column it is shown that in Naba tone attaches to moras rather than to syllables. [p. 95] ... 8 LHL is almost exclusively found in Chadian Arabic loan words, reflecting the stress system of that language. [fn. 8, p. 97]
new_statements.citation: Scherrer, Elaine Marie. 2022. A phonological description of Naba. Afrika und Übersee 95: 76-134. DOI 10.15460/auue.2022.95.1.255
new_statements.locator: Section 4 'Tone', p. 95 (pdf page 21); footnote 8, p. 97 (pdf page 23)
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given: the only phonological description that could be opened treats Naba as a three-level tone language (H, M, L on moras; nine lexical melodies, M commonest, HL commonest overall; toneless clitics/affixes) and never mentions word stress or accent in Naba. The one use of 'stress' (fn. 8) refers to the stress system of Chadian Arabic as the origin of an LHL melody in loanwords.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal notes: MH and LHL melodies are rare, LHL confined to Chadian Arabic loans; HH sequences restricted; downstep and tone spreading described (4.4).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (word-level) tone melodies on nouns and verbs; analysis based on citation forms and short phrases (plural =ge clitic used to reveal underlying melodies); author states the tone analysis is 'incomplete' and grammatical tone still under study (p. 78). Describes the Yao sub-dialect of Bilala.
new_statements.identity_note: Scherrer 2022 treats Naba (= Bilala/Kuka/Medogo; community name 'Melbene') as a single language (citing Maass 2001) and describes the Yao sub-dialect of the Bilala dialect (main informant from Yao; p. 77-78). Glottolog naba1253 has no separate dialect codes listed on the fetched sources page; the Bilala sub-dialects (Yao, Ambassatna, Amjamena-bilala, Moeto) are speaker-acknowledged only. The earlier scan's 'NO-SOURCE-FOUND' verdict was wrong: Glottolog 5.1 lists Scherrer 2022 (hhtype phonology) and it is open access.

sources.locator: Section 4 'Tone', p. 95 (pdf page 21); footnote 8, p. 97 (pdf page 23)
sources.note: Full segmental + tonal phonology (sections 2-6). Section 4 'Tone' (p. 95) states Naba is a tonal language with three level tones H, M, L attaching to moras; nine tone melodies; toneless grammatical morphemes. There is no stress/accent/prominence section and no statement about word stress in Naba anywhere in the 60 pages; the single occurrence of 'stress' is footnote 8 (p. 97), which attributes the rare LHL melody of Chadian Arabic loanwords to 'the stress system of that language' (Arabic), not to Naba. Dialect described: Yao sub-dialect of Bilala (p. 77-78).
Bibliographic only: live page lists Bombay 2010 (sociolinguistic) and Ethnologue 2025; the Glottolog 5.1 dump used by WORLD_TARGETS additionally lists Scherrer 2022, Adama Dacour 2001 and Laya 2003.
